chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a person in i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) who had intercourse with his wife. He said: 'Upon him is what is upon the one who deliberately broke his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan: freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people.' If the intercourse was at night during the month of Ramadan, then upon the one who had intercourse is one expiation; and if it was during the day, then upon him are two expiations. He narrated that.

key_terms.مُعْتَكِفٍ: A person in i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque for worship)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for sexual intercourse during i'tikaf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that sexual intercourse during i'tikaf incurs the same expiation (kaffarah) as breaking the fast deliberately, reflecting the sanctity of the sacred space. It distinguishes between night and day occurrences, with daytime acts requiring double expiation due to the concurrent violation of the day's fast, a nuance rooted in the jurisprudential principle that i'tikaf is an extension of fasting. This ruling underscores the continuity of ritual purity and devotion required within the mosque precincts.
